court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Court of Civil Judge, Senior Division, Kalyan (HMP Case No.777/2014)
case_name: Mrs Krutika Ritesh Arya vs Ritesh Laxman Arya
facts_of_case: The applicant and respondent were married in 2012. The applicant left her matrimonial home due to harassment by the respondent and his family members. She delivered a baby boy out of wedlock in 2013. The respondent filed a petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking indulgence to show that no prejudice would be caused to the other party.
legal_principles.held: In so far as the submission of the learned counsel for the respondent that the applicant can be paid reasonable amount on transportation of the applicant from Nashik to Kalyan and no prejudice would be caused to the applicant is concerned, in my view, merely because the respondent has offered to pay reasonable expenses on transportation will not be sufficient for the applicant to leave her 2 years and 11 months old child with her old parents for attending the Court.
cited_cases: Kalpana Deviprakash Thakar Vs.Dr.Deviprakash Thakar, (1996) 11 SCC 96

legal_principles.principle: The court will not grant indulgence to a party who is not willing to make reasonable arrangements for the other party's attendance at Court proceedings.
legal_principles.held: It is not in dispute that the child of the applicant and the respondent is hardly 2 years and 11 months old who is staying with the applicant. Medical reports annexed to the application by the applicant clearly indicate that the applicant has been suffering from various ailments and Post Pregnancy complications.

outcome.final_order: The applicant's application for transfer of the petition to the Family Court at Nashik was allowed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition in family court
advising on divorce proceedings in India
preparing a case for harassment allegations
